note: Strong on every axis: faithful, scoped, grounded, names the signal.
subject: Billed twice this morning
body: I was charged twice for order 4471 today, two identical entries on the card ending 4242.
summary: Customer double-charged for order 4471; two identical entries on card ending 4242.
reasoning: Money moved incorrectly (a duplicate charge), so this is billing and the escalation rule fires. High, not critical: one order on one account and the amount is recoverable.

note: Faithful but vague summary: restates the category, gives no scope.
subject: Problem with my bill
body: There is something wrong on my latest invoice, the total looks higher than I expected.
reasoning: The invoice total looks wrong to the customer, so this is billing. A human should check the actual charge.

note: Adversarial: summary invents an amount and a date the ticket never gives.
subject: Refund not received
body: I asked for a refund last week and it still has not arrived. Can you check?
summary: Customer awaiting a $250 refund requested 10 days ago.
reasoning: A refund is outstanding, so this is billing. Route to a human to verify the refund status.

note: Adversarial: reasoning fabricates a cause not present in the ticket.
subject: App is slow
body: The dashboard has been really slow to load for the past two days.
summary: Dashboard load times have degraded for the customer over the past two days.
reasoning: The slowness is caused by the customer's recent data import overloading their workspace, so this is expected behaviour and low priority.

note: Faithful and actionable summary, but circular reasoning that names no signal.
subject: Cannot log in
body: None of my team can log in since this morning, we just get an error page.
summary: Whole team unable to log in since this morning, seeing an error page.
reasoning: This is an account access problem because it is about logging in.

note: Strong: precise summary, reasoning names the deciding facts.
subject: 503s on the events API
body: Since 09:15 UTC every POST to /v1/events returns a 503. We have retried from three regions.
summary: All POSTs to /v1/events returning 503 since 09:15 UTC, reproduced from three regions.
reasoning: Total loss of a core endpoint with no workaround, so critical and escalate. Reproduction across three regions rules out a client-side cause.

note: Mediocre: summary drops the specifics, reasoning stays generic.
subject: Export question
body: Is there a way to export my reports to Excel? I can only find CSV.
summary: Customer wants a new export feature.
reasoning: This is a feature request, so route it to a human.

note: Adversarial: faithful summary, but reasoning invents a benign cause and waves it away.
subject: Missing records
body: About 400 records that were there yesterday are gone this morning. They are not in trash.
summary: About 400 records missing since yesterday, not found in trash.
reasoning: The records were likely deleted by another admin on the customer's team, so no action is needed on our side.

note: Strong, with the PII signal named explicitly.
subject: Help with a failed import
body: The import keeps failing. Here is a sample row: Jane Doe, jane.doe@acme.com, +1-555-0199, 4111 1111 1111 1111.
summary: Customer's data import fails; a pasted sample row contains a name, email, phone and full card number.
reasoning: An import failure is technical. The pasted row is a third party's PII including a full card number, so contains_pii is true and the body must be redacted before it is forwarded.

note: Weak: summary restates the mood, reasoning is circular.
subject: Unhappy
body: I have been a customer for years and I am really not happy with how things are going lately.
reasoning: This is a complaint because the customer is complaining.
